name: LEBANON
lead: Lebanon is a small Mediterranean country with 6,000 years of history. Phoenician ships carried the world's first alphabet from here. Snowy peaks rise an hour from sunny beaches. You can ski and swim on the same winter day.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Lebanon runs in four north–south stripes. First comes a sunny Mediterranean coast, then Mount Lebanon. Next is the flat Bekaa Valley, then the Anti-Lebanon mountains on the Syrian border.
The Kadisha Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Monks once sheltered in its cliff caves. Cedar groves above 1,400 m hold trees over a thousand years old.
animals: The Lebanon cedar is the national emblem. Ancient trees in the Shouf reserve spread flat canopies like giant green parasols. Striped hyenas, wild boar and stone martens roam the forests at night.
Loggerhead sea turtles nest on Lebanon's sandy beaches each summer. Every autumn, flocks of honey buzzards and short-toed eagles funnel through the mountain ridges.
culture: Lebanese meals begin with meze: hummus, tabbouleh and warm flatbread. Guests get cardamom coffee the moment they arrive. Hospitality is a point of national pride.
Dabke is a stomping line dance performed at weddings. Dancers link arms and kick in time. Baalbeck's festival has held opera and jazz inside colossal Roman ruins since 1956.
history: Phoenicians founded trading cities here around 3000 BCE. They spread the first widely used alphabet to Greece. Alexander the Great, Romans, Crusaders and Ottomans each left temples and castles.
Lebanon gained independence from France in 1943. A civil war (1975–1990) split Beirut along the Green Line, but the city rebuilt. Baalbek's Roman temples have stood for 2,000 years.
wows: Phoenicians invented the 22-letter alphabet behind Greek, Latin and Arabic.
Mzaar ski slopes and Mediterranean beaches are just 50 km apart.
Baalbek's Trilithon holds three stones weighing up to 1,000 tonnes each.
Byblos has been inhabited since about 5000 BCE.
About 14 million Lebanese live abroad, over double the home population.
Alexander's causeway to Tyre, built in 332 BCE, still stands.
Egyptian pharaohs sent fleets to Lebanon to buy cedar wood.

myths.myth: Royal purple dye came from plants
myths.fact: Phoenicians made purple dye from sea snails. Thousands of snails gave only a little dye.

myths.myth: The first alphabet had vowels like A and E
myths.fact: The Phoenician alphabet had only consonants. The Greeks later added vowels.
